To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the oxidative stress status can be evaluated by measuring the level of oxidized proteins in plasma, and that it is possible to decrease the oxidative damage in proteins by consuming a diet rich in antioxidants.

Oxidative stress, which is defined as an unbalance between the production of ROS and the antioxidant network in favor of the former, is associated with the risk of developing ageing-related pathologies such as cancer and cardiovascular diseases.
the oxidative stress status is an important factor in the pathophysiology of ageing and age-related pathologies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of oxidative stress in order to better understand its pathophysiological mechanisms and its role in the onset of diseases.
the identification of biomarkers of oxidative stress, in order to better understand the mechanisms involved in the development of pathologies and to develop new therapeutic targets.
the development of new methods for the determination of oxidative stress in biological systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the oxidative stress is a major player in the development of ageing and age related diseases.

the oxidative stress is an important contributor to the pathogenesis of a number of chronic diseases and that the measurement of the oxidative stress is a useful tool to evaluate the risk of developing such diseases.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the oxidative stress status in an individual can be evidenced by measuring the level of the oxidative stress biomarker 8-oxo-7,8-dihydro-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-oxo-dG) in urine and in DNA.
we have developed a technology allowing the measurement of oxidative stress at the cellular level.

we are developing an innovative technology based on the use of fluorescent probes for the detection and quantification of the oxidative damage in the different biological targets (lipids, proteins and DNA) and the use of these probes in the development of a diagnostic test for oxidative stress status.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a high sensitive method to measure the oxidation of DNA, proteins and fatty acids in a single sample, allows a better assessment of the oxidative stress status in a population, compared with the use of a single biomarker.
we have developed an innovative method for the quantification of the oxidative damages of lipids, proteins and DNA, based on the measurement of their oxidation products.
the use of the OxyBlot® technology allows to correctly identify oxidative damage in DNA and proteins.
